description: Detailed convention configurations for 14 physics subfields — the default reference for physics convention locks

natural_units.description: ℏ = c = 1. All quantities expressed in powers of energy. Mass in GeV, length in GeV⁻¹, time in GeV⁻¹.

metric_signature.description: g_μν = diag(+1, -1, -1, -1). Timelike vectors have positive norm. Used in Peskin & Schroeder, Weinberg QFT.

consequences.kinetic_term: Positive kinetic energy: ∂_μ φ ∂^μ φ has correct sign
consequences.on_shell_condition: p² = p_μ p^μ = m² > 0 for timelike

fourier_convention.description: Forward: f̃(k) = ∫ d⁴x f(x) exp(+ik·x). Inverse: f(x) = ∫ d⁴k/(2π)⁴ f̃(k) exp(-ik·x). The 2π factors all in the inverse transform.

renormalization_scheme.description: Renormalization conditions imposed at physical particle masses. Propagator pole at physical mass with residue 1. Used in Peskin & Schroeder Chapter 10.

consequences.pole_condition: Propagator pole at p² = m²_ph (physical mass)
consequences.counterterms: Defined to cancel divergences at physical mass point

gauge_choice.description: ∂_μ A^μ = 0 gauge fixing. Propagator: D_μν(k) = -i(g_μν - k_μ k_ν/k²)/(k²+iε) + gauge terms. ξ parameter in general Lorentz gauge.

coordinate_system.description: Flat spacetime with Cartesian coordinates. ds² = dt² - dx² - dy² - dz² (mostly-minus).

spin_statistics.description: Integer spin → commutation relations → Bose-Einstein statistics. Half-integer spin → anticommutation relations → Fermi-Dirac statistics.

consequences.fermion_partition: Z_F = 1 + exp(-βE) for single fermion mode

lagrangian_sign.description: L = T - V with positive kinetic energy term. Standard convention in most QFT textbooks.

mostly_minus_to_mostly_plus.description: To convert results from mostly-minus to mostly-plus signature
transformations: γ matrices: γ^μ → same but contraction sign flips

natural_to_SI.description: To convert from natural units (ℏ=c=1) to SI
transformations: Restore ℏ, c factors by dimensional analysis

physics_to_math_fourier.description: To convert between physics and mathematical Fourier conventions
transformations: Physics → Math: multiply forward transform by (2π)^(d/2)
Math → Physics: divide forward transform by (2π)^(d/2)
Math: 2π split symmetrically between forward and inverse

on_shell_to_MS_bar.description: To convert between on-shell and MS-bar renormalization schemes
transformations: Finite parts differ; divergent parts same (both cancel poles)

natural_units.description: ℏ = 1 but c is often irrelevant (low-energy regime). Energy in eV or meV. Temperature in Kelvin with kB explicitly included or absorbed.

conversion_rules.temperature: kB × T: at 300K, kB T ≈ 25.8 meV

metric_signature.description: g_ij = diag(+1, +1, +1) for spatial metric in Euclidean formulation. Imaginary-time formalism: dt → i dτ, τ is real.

consequences.euclidean_action: S_E = ∫ dτ d³x [T + V] with positive real action
consequences.propagator: G(τ) = ⟨O(τ)O(0)⟩, decays exponentially for gapped systems

fourier_convention.description: Same as QFT physics convention but restricted to spatial+imaginary-time: f̃(k, iωn) = ∫ dτ d³x f(τ,x) exp(+ik·x - iωn τ).

gauge_choice.description: ∇·A = 0 gauge. Separates longitudinal and transverse photon modes. Convenient for condensed matter where static Coulomb interaction dominates.

consequences.coulomb_potential: V(r) = e²/(4π r) from instantaneous Coulomb term

matsubara.description: Bosonic: ωn = 2nπ/β. Fermionic: ωn = (2n+1)π/β. Standard finite-temperature imaginary-time formalism.

consequences.contour: Sum → contour integral via Matsubara poles

coordinate_system.description: Euclidean 3D spatial coordinates. Most condensed matter calculations in flat space.

spin_statistics.description: Standard spin-statistics: bosons (phonons, magnons) commute; fermions (electrons, holes) anticommute.

lagrangian_sign.description: L = T - V. Positive kinetic energy for stable condensed matter systems.

natural_units.description: kB = 1. Temperature in energy units. All thermodynamic quantities in units of kB or energy.

conversion_rules.entropy: S in units of kB (dimensionless when kB=1)

metric_signature.description: Standard 4D signature when relativistic stat mech is needed (e.g., QFT thermal field theory).

fourier_convention.description: Standard physics Fourier for partition functions and correlation functions.

matsubara.description: Bosonic: ωn = 2nπ/β. Fermionic: ωn = (2n+1)π/β. Standard imaginary-time Matsubara formalism.

coordinate_system.description: Flat Euclidean space for most stat mech problems.

natural_units.description: G = c = 1. All quantities in units of length (or mass via Schwarzschild radius). Common in GR and cosmology.

conversion_rules.mass: M [m] → M × c²/G [kg], Schwarzschild radius rs = 2M

metric_signature.description: g_μν = diag(-1, +1, +1, +1). Spacelike vectors have positive norm. Used in MTW Gravitation, Carroll Spacetime & Geometry.

consequences.ricci_scalar: R = g^μν R_μν with this sign convention

fourier_convention.description: Physics Fourier convention for cosmological perturbation analysis and mode expansions.

gauge_choice.description: Harmonic/de Donder gauge: ∇_μ (∇^μ h^ν_ρ - 1/2 ∇^ρ h) = 0. Used for linearized GR and cosmological perturbation theory.

consequences.linearized_gr: Simplifies wave equation for metric perturbations

coordinate_system.description: General coordinates with arbitrary metric g_μν(x). Coordinate freedom is the gauge freedom in GR.

lagrangian_sign.description: Einstein-Hilbert action S = (1/16π) ∫ d⁴x √(-g) R + matter terms. Positive sign for GR.

mostly_plus_to_mostly_minus.description: To convert results from mostly-plus to mostly-minus signature
transformations: Ricci scalar sign: R → -R (sign flip in some definitions)
Einstein tensor: sign conventions may differ

geometric_to_SI.description: To convert from geometric units (G=c=1) to SI
transformations: Restore G, c factors by dimensional analysis

natural_units.description: Hartree energy Eh = me e⁴/(4π ε₀)² ℏ² = 27.2 eV. Bohr radius a₀ = ℏ²/(me e²) = 0.529 Å. ℏ = 1, me = 1, e = 1, 4πε₀ = 1.

metric_signature.description: Standard Minkowski signature for relativistic atomic calculations. Most AMO work uses non-relativistic Schrödinger (Euclidean).

fourier_convention.description: Physics Fourier for transition amplitude calculations.

gauge_choice.description: ∇·A = 0. The Coulomb gauge is natural for atomic physics — the Coulomb interaction is instantaneous and dominant.

consequences.coulomb: V(r) = Ze²/(4π ε₀ r) — instantaneous Coulomb potential

coordinate_system.description: Cartesian coordinates for most atomic structure calculations. Spherical for angular momentum.

spin_statistics.description: Standard: electrons are fermions, photons are bosons.

lagrangian_sign.description: L = T - V. Standard for atomic Hamiltonian with bound states.

atomic_to_SI.description: To convert from atomic units to SI
transformations: Restore me, e, ℏ, ε₀ by dimensional analysis

natural_units.description: ℏ = c = 1. Energy in GeV (particle physics) or MeV (nuclear physics). Standard HEP convention.

metric_signature.description: g_μν = diag(+1, -1, -1, -1). Standard HEP convention (PDG, Peskin & Schroeder).

fourier_convention.description: Physics Fourier. Standard in particle physics for amplitude calculations.

renormalization_scheme.description: Modified minimal subtraction. Subtract only divergent 1/ε poles plus universal constants (ln 4π - γE). Standard for collider phenomenology.

consequences.running_coupling: αs(μ) runs according to MS-bar β-function
consequences.scale_dependence: Physical observables independent of μ after proper RG evolution
consequences.scheme_conversion: MS-bar → on-shell: finite shift at each order

gauge_choice.description: ∂_μ A^μ = 0. Standard for perturbative QCD calculations.

coordinate_system.description: Flat Minkowski spacetime for collider physics. S-matrix defined asymptotically.

spin_statistics.description: Standard spin-statistics for all particle species.

lagrangian_sign.description: Standard L = T - V for QCD/QED Lagrangian.

MS_bar_to_on_shell.description: To convert between MS-bar and on-shell renormalization schemes
transformations: m_MS_bar²(μ) → m_OS² via finite shift at each perturbative order
α_MS_bar(μ) → α_OS via scheme conversion factor
Different finite parts; same UV pole structure

natural_units.description: Dimensionless. Information-theoretic quantities (qubits, entropy) are naturally dimensionless.

angular_momentum.description: Spin-1/2 represented as |0⟩, |1⟩ qubit basis. No physical angular momentum units.

spin_statistics.description: Qubit convention: states labeled |0⟩ and |1⟩, NOT |↑⟩/|↓⟩. Computational basis preferred.

natural_units.description: SI units required for fluid dynamics and plasma physics — dimensional quantities (viscosity ν, diffusivity D, plasma frequency ωp) must retain physical dimensions.

metric_signature.description: Standard for relativistic MHD and plasma calculations in Minkowski spacetime.

fourier_convention.description: Physics Fourier for spectral decomposition of fluid fields.

coordinate_system.description: Cartesian coordinates for most fluid/plasma calculations. Curvilinear (cylindrical/spherical) for specific geometries.

lagrangian_sign.description: Standard Lagrangian for fluid equations (Euler, Navier-Stokes).

natural_units.description: ℏ = c = 1. Common for algebraic and structural analysis where physical dimensions are secondary.

metric_signature.description: Standard physics signature for operator algebra and C*-algebraic QFT.

fourier_convention.description: Mathematical Fourier: f̃(k) = (2π)^(-d/2) ∫ f(x) exp(-ik·x) dx. Symmetric normalization. Common in mathematical physics and analysis.

consequences.normalization: Both forward and inverse transform have (2π)^(-d/2) factor

coordinate_system.description: General manifold coordinates. Mathematical physics often works on arbitrary manifolds.

angular_momentum.description: Abstract representation theory (Lie algebra su(2), Clebsch-Gordan coefficients as abstract operators). No specific physical realization.

lagrangian_sign.description: Standard sign convention for variational formulations.

math_to_physics_fourier.description: To convert between mathematical and physics Fourier conventions
transformations: Math → Physics: divide forward transform by (2π)^(d/2)
Physics → Math: multiply forward transform by (2π)^(d/2)
Consequence: Plancherel theorem differs by (2π)^d factor

natural_units.description: Solar mass M☉ = 1.978×10³⁰ kg. AU = 1.496×10¹¹ m. Year = 3.156×10⁷ s. Luminosity in L☉. G and c kept explicit.

metric_signature.description: g_μν = diag(-1, +1, +1, +1). Common in astrophysics/GR literature (Carroll, MTW).

fourier_convention.description: Physics Fourier for spectral analysis and cosmological perturbation theory.

coordinate_system.description: General coordinates for curved spacetime (Schwarzschild, FRW cosmology).

astronomical_to_SI.description: To convert from astronomical units to SI
transformations: Distance: d [AU] → d × 1.496×10¹¹ m, d [pc] → d × 3.086×10¹⁶ m

natural_units.description: kB = 1. Length in units of persistence length ℓp or monomer size a. Time in units of relaxation time τ. Temperature T in energy units.

fourier_convention.description: Physics Fourier for scattering (S(k)) and correlation function analysis.

matsubara.description: Standard Matsubara for polymer field theory and liquid structure calculations.

coordinate_system.description: Euclidean 3D for soft matter. No spacetime structure needed.

natural_units.description: ℏ = c = 1. Algebraic structures (operator algebras, C*-algebras) work best in dimensionless/natural units.

metric_signature.description: g_μν = diag(+1, -1, -1, -1). Standard for Wightman axioms and Haag-Kastler nets.

fourier_convention.description: Physics Fourier for operator-valued distributions and tempered distributions.

coordinate_system.description: Minkowski spacetime for algebraic QFT axioms (Wightman, Haag-Kastler).

angular_momentum.description: Abstract representation theory. Clebsch-Gordan as abstract algebraic objects.

spin_statistics.description: Spin-statistics theorem as algebraic axiom (proof via locality and positivity).

lagrangian_sign.description: Standard sign convention for variational/algebraic formulations.

natural_units.description: ℏ = c = 1. String length α' = 1/(2π) or α' = 1 depending on convention. Most SFT calculations in natural units.

conversion_rules.string_length: α' = ls² where ls is fundamental string length

metric_signature.description: g_μν = diag(+1, -1, -1, -1). Standard for worldsheet and target space metrics in string theory.

fourier_convention.description: Physics Fourier for worldsheet mode expansions and target space amplitudes.

gauge_choice.description: Lorentz gauge for string field theory (Witten's OSFT). Also: conformal gauge on worldsheet.

consequences.worldsheet: Conformal gauge: h_ab = e^φ η_ab on worldsheet
consequences.target_space: Lorentz gauge for open string field theory cubic action

coordinate_system.description: Minkowski target space for perturbative string theory. AdS or other curved backgrounds for non-perturbative.

lagrangian_sign.description: Positive kinetic term for string field theory action. S = (1/2)⟨Φ|Q|Φ⟩ + (g/3)⟨Φ|Φ|Φ⟩.

natural_units.description: SI units for classical mechanics. Force in Newtons, energy in Joules, length in meters.

fourier_convention.description: Physics Fourier for wave mechanics and signal analysis in classical systems.

coordinate_system.description: Cartesian coordinates for Newtonian mechanics. Generalized coordinates for Lagrangian/Hamiltonian.

angular_momentum.description: Classical angular momentum L = r × p. No quantization. Values are continuous (integer only for quantized systems).

lagrangian_sign.description: L = T - V. Standard classical mechanics Lagrangian.
